4th Period.workingNow: Joining SchoolAI with the class code and asking it one question.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A new 'My Thoughts on AI' page live on your portfolio site — your written opinion (with reasoning) plus at least one image, pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can explain how AI predicts an answer from training data so that I understand what's actually happening when I use a tool like SchoolAI.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.DA.5 — Analyze data using computational tools in order to make claims and predictions.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: I do: how AI predicts a 'next best answer' from data (8 min)
We do: join SchoolAI, test the class code together (8 min)
You do: ask SchoolAI one question, screenshot the reply (8 min)
Exit Ticket: one thing that surprised you (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you defined what AI is. Today you get your hands on one — SchoolAI — and see how it actually decides what to say back to you. Tomorrow we look at what can go wrong when people trust that answer too much.

6th Period.workingNow: Picking two aesthetics — feelings — you want your game to give players, and explaining why.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: MDA framework notes (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) + a one-page Game Design Plan for your SchoolAI game, shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can name the aesthetic — the feeling — I want my game to give players so that my design choices have a clear purpose.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: I do: what feeling should players have? (6 min)
We do: name a shared game's aesthetic as a class (6 min)
You do: pick 2 aesthetics for your game & explain why (12 min)
Exit Ticket: your game's one-word feeling (2 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday you listed mechanics — the rules and pieces. Today's the easy one: what should your game actually feel like to play? Tomorrow's the hard part — figuring out how those rules create that feeling.
